papers.title: Reference Forcing: Long Video Generation with Region-Guided Drift Correction
papers.abstract: Long video generation should keep the subject and background consistent while supporting rich, natural motion. However, autoregressive models are often distilled with distribution matching distillation (DMD) over short windows, which does not train them to keep this consistency over long ranges. As a result, the subject and background can drift over time. Methods that manage the key-value (KV) cache retain or retrieve history to reduce drift. Yet this history may itself have drifted. We propose Reference Forcing, which uses the initial frames as an appearance reference. We first build a teacher that uses attention masks to force each region of a new frame to attend to the same region in the initial frames. The teacher finds these regions with off-the-shelf segmentation models. We then distill this behavior into a separate attention path of the student, which needs no external models at inference. We further introduce value correction, which corrects drifted values in the KV cache toward the matching values of drift-free initial frames. Experiments show that Reference Forcing achieves state-of-the-art subject and background consistency among long-video methods on different base models, and its advantage grows with video length. Ablations show both components are needed to gain consistency without losing motion. More visualizations and code are available at https://zhaosheng-thu.github.io/reference-force/
papers.summary_cn: 论文针对自回归长视频生成中的主体和背景外观随时间漂移问题，提出Reference Forcing。该方法以初始视频块为稳定外观参考，通过教师模型中的区域掩码注意力学习主体和背景的对应关系，并将其蒸馏为无需外部模型的独立锚点注意力路径；同时利用学习到的锚点门控，对KV缓存中较早、已漂移的值进行匹配和校正。实验基于LongLive和Self-Forcing，在一致性、运动和画质等指标上进行比较，结果显示该方法显著提升长时域主体与背景一致性，并在保持运动的同时优于多种缓存、检索和位置编码方法。其局限包括仅使用首个视频块作为参考、后续出现的内容缺乏参考、画质略低于基础模型，以及相似多主体场景和主体检测失败场景仍较困难。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出区域引导蒸馏方法：教师模型借助主体分割和背景光流构造区域注意力掩码，使当前帧区域关注初始帧中的对应区域，并将该行为蒸馏到学生模型的独立锚点注意力路径中。2. 引入可学习的锚点门控，使已出现在初始帧中的内容使用外观参考，而新出现的内容减少或关闭锚点注意力，从而兼顾一致性与运动。3. 提出无需训练的值校正机制，利用KV键空间中的互为最近邻匹配，将近期缓存中的漂移值向初始帧对应值插值修正，同时保留键并避免校正最新块造成闪烁。4. 在LongLive和Self-Forcing基础模型上进行广泛实验，证明该方法能够提升长视频主体和背景一致性，并在较长生成时域中保持优势。
papers.relevance_cn: 该工作与视频生成和视频扩散高度相关，直接面向自回归视频扩散模型的长视频生成。它通过KV缓存管理、初始帧锚定、独立注意力路径和缓存值复用来抑制长时域误差累积，涉及因果、自回归和流式分块生成。方法在推理阶段不依赖外部分割或光流模型，适合实时或低额外开销的长视频生成；但论文没有提出新的蒸馏加速或稀疏注意力机制，重点是利用缓存校正和区域引导提高时序外观一致性，而非动作条件视觉世界模型或闭环模拟。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出：方法只使用初始视频块作为参考，因此后续才出现的物体没有可用参考，动态更新参考内容留待未来研究；锚点路径会对初始帧匹配区域进行平均，可能轻微平滑细粒度纹理，使成像质量略低于LongLive；包含多个相似主体的场景仍然困难，因为教师使用的分割流程只跟踪单个主体；教师依赖主体检测器，若检测不到主体，就会将整个画面视为背景并通过光流匹配，这在风景或人群等没有明显主体的场景中更常见。论文未明确说明该方法在更大规模基础模型、更多样化摄像机运动、真实世界视频或超长于两小时的视频上的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_cn: 长视频生成应在支持丰富、自然运动的同时，保持主体和背景的一致性。然而，自回归模型通常在短窗口上通过分布匹配蒸馏（DMD）进行蒸馏训练，这使其没有学会在较长范围内维持这种一致性。因此，主体和背景会随时间发生漂移。管理键值（KV）缓存的方法会保留或检索历史信息，以减少漂移，但这些历史信息本身可能已经发生漂移。我们提出 Reference Forcing，使用初始帧作为外观参考。首先，我们构建一个教师模型，利用注意力掩码强制新帧的每个区域关注初始帧中的同一区域。教师模型使用现成的分割模型寻找这些区域。随后，我们将这种行为蒸馏到学生模型的一条独立注意力路径中，使其在推理时不需要外部模型。进一步地，我们引入值校正，将KV缓存中已经漂移的值向无漂移初始帧中的匹配值修正。实验表明，在不同基础模型上的长视频方法中，Reference Forcing在主体和背景一致性方面达到了现有最佳水平，并且其优势会随着视频长度增加而扩大。消融实验表明，两个组件都是在不损失运动的情况下提升一致性所必需的。更多可视化结果和代码见 https://zhaosheng-thu.github.io/reference-force/。

papers.title: FastFrames: Video Generation at Interactive Latency
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models generate frames based on new observations and inputs, making them a promising medium for interactive visual experiences. However, existing models are orders of magnitude too slow for fluid interaction. This paper introduces FastFrames, a family of fast autoregressive video diffusion models that achieves interactive latency without compromising quality. We profile the inference pipeline of state-of-the-art models and find that operations often treated as fixed implementation details, such as VAE decoding and KV cache updates, in fact account for over half of end-to-end inference latency. We challenge the assumption that these components are indispensable and replace them with lightweight alternatives. Our 1.3B variant runs at 36 ms per frame, or 28 responses per second (RPS), on a single B200 GPU while matching the generation quality of a state-of-the-art model that is nearly 8x slower. Our 14B variant runs at 45 ms per frame, or 22 RPS, on an 8x B200 GPU node and yields significantly better visual quality and realism. We show that FastFrames enables real-time interaction in applications such as camera-conditioned and physics-conditioned video generation.
papers.summary_cn: 本文针对自回归视频扩散模型端到端响应速度过慢的问题，提出 FastFrames。作者通过延迟剖析发现，VAE 解码和 KV 缓存更新等非去噪操作是主要瓶颈，因此分别使用轻量级 ConvNeXt 像素解码器和 KV 修复网络替代原组件，并结合持久化缓存、分段注意力、算子融合、CUDA Graph 及上下文并行等系统优化。在 480p 条件下，1.3B 模型单 GPU 达到 36 毫秒/帧，14B 模型 8 GPU 达到 45 毫秒/帧，同时保持与基线相当或更好的 VBench 质量。优化也被迁移到相机条件和物理条件模型，使其响应延迟接近交互目标。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 提出以端到端每帧延迟和每秒响应数衡量交互式视频生成性能，并将 50 毫秒（20 RPS）作为目标。 2. 设计轻量级 ConvNeXt 像素解码器，将 VAE 解码延迟从 147 毫秒降至约 1 毫秒，同时保持视觉细节和质量。 3. 提出 KV 修复网络，以轻量网络预测干净潜变量对应的缓存修正，将 KV 更新开销大幅降低。 4. 结合持久化 KV 缓存、预计算条件、融合 QKV 投影、分段注意力、CUDA Graph 和多 GPU 上下文并行，降低 DiT 推理延迟。 5. 构建 1.3B 和 14B 的 FastFrames 模型，在交互延迟范围内达到具有竞争力的生成质量，并验证其对相机条件和物理条件视频模型的加速效果。
papers.relevance_cn: 论文与研究重点高度相关。它直接研究自回归、因果、流式视频生成的实时推理，针对每个新输入到首个受影响 RGB 帧呈现之间的延迟进行优化。其方法涉及视频扩散加速、少步蒸馏模型的端到端优化、KV 缓存复用与快速更新、稀疏/分段注意力、硬件感知并行以及高效像素解码。通过相机条件和物理条件生成实验，论文还与动作或控制条件视觉世界模型及闭环交互仿真相关；不过其主要定量评测仍集中在文本到视频生成，而不是完整的闭环世界模型任务。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文明确指出，评测主要集中于 480p 文本到视频生成，并依赖高端 B200 GPU；未来仍需支持更高分辨率和更轻量的硬件形态。作者还指出，加入动作条件而不增加延迟、改善长期一致性和物理合理性是尚未解决的问题。相机条件和物理条件模型经过优化后仍比文本到视频模型更慢，部分原因是需要更多扩散步、每个自回归步骤预测多个潜在帧，并处理额外条件。与可跨同系列模型共享的通用 VAE 不同，像素解码器需要针对每个模型分别微调。论文未明确说明更长视频时长、复杂闭环控制场景和广泛硬件平台上的性能。
papers.abstract_cn: 自回归视频扩散模型根据新的观测和输入生成帧，因此有望成为交互式视觉体验的理想媒介。然而，现有模型的速度通常比流畅交互所需的速度慢几个数量级。本文提出 FastFrames，一系列无需牺牲质量即可实现交互延迟的快速自回归视频扩散模型。我们对当前最先进模型的推理流程进行了分析，发现通常被视为固定实现细节的操作（例如 VAE 解码和 KV 缓存更新）实际上占据了端到端推理延迟的一半以上。我们质疑这些组件是否不可或缺，并以轻量级替代方案取代它们。我们的 1.3B 版本在单个 B200 GPU 上每帧运行时间为 36 毫秒，即每秒 28 次响应（RPS），同时保持了与一个速度几乎慢 8 倍的先进模型相当的生成质量。我们的 14B 版本在由 8 个 B200 GPU 组成的节点上每帧运行时间为 45 毫秒，即 22 RPS，并呈现出显著更好的视觉质量和真实感。我们展示了 FastFrames 如何支持相机条件和物理条件视频生成等应用中的实时交互。

papers.title: SAFER: Navigating the Exploration-Exploitation Dilemma in World-Model-Based Planning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: An autonomous vehicle must foresee the consequences of its actions, especially in the rare, time-critical situations where crashes happen. A world model offers this foresight, but only within the coverage of its training data, which poses an exploration-exploitation dilemma. Within this coverage a planner can hardly improve on the data, and beyond it the model's errors mislead it. Logs of competent driving rarely contain the failures that would widen the coverage, and agents that learn from interaction gain them only by failing themselves, without being shown what to do instead. We propose SAFER, a framework that learns offline from failures that others make, judged by an expert, and keeps learning online from its own driving. Offline, partially trained agents and scripted, recoverable perturbations Stage failures in simulation, and an expert Annotates every visited state with its action and value, so that much of what the planner explores is covered before it drives. In planning, a chunked latent world model Foresees the consequences fast enough for real-time use, and a risk-aware sampling-based planner Evaluates candidate maneuvers by their return minus a bounded collision penalty. Online, a loop continuously Refines the model wherever this driving leaves the coverage of the offline data. In closed-loop evaluation against the compared methods, SAFER reaches the highest route completion and reward per step on the CARLA Leaderboard routes, 0.95 and 0.77 from a privileged bird's-eye view, and the highest episode reward in MetaDrive, 53.4 in regular and 49.0 in safety-critical traffic. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/safer-website.
papers.summary_cn: 论文研究依赖世界模型进行自动驾驶规划时的探索—利用困境：模型在训练数据覆盖范围内较可靠但难以超越数据，超出覆盖范围后又会因模型误差偏向错误的高估动作。SAFER通过三个环节缓解该问题。首先，在仿真中利用能力较弱的驾驶策略和脚本化可恢复扰动制造失败，并由专家为每个状态提供正确动作和值标签，使世界模型同时学习错误行为的后果和应采取的恢复动作。其次，构建带有分块潜在动力学、奖励与价值预测、行为克隆动作先验及碰撞风险头的世界模型，并用风险感知MPPI对候选动作块进行实时规划。该模型以因果掩码一次性预测未来16步潜变量，规划器每0.1秒重规划并执行首个动作。最后，模型在线根据自身驾驶数据适应动力学、奖励评分器和风险头，利用离线数据混合训练及指数移动平均目标保持规划目标稳定。CARLA和MetaDrive的闭环实验表明，风险惩罚、在线适应和针对覆盖不足场景的数据飞轮均能提升整体表现；SAFER在CARLA上取得0.95路线完成率和0.80驾驶得分，在MetaDrive常规及安全关键交通中分别取得53.4和49.0的回合回报。
papers.contribution_cn: 1. 形式化描述了世界模型规划中的探索—利用困境，并通过模型误差与规划遗憾分析说明，最大化模型预测值会使规划器偏向模型高估的候选动作。2. 提出由他人制造、专家标注的失败数据构建方案：使用部分训练的智能体、动作噪声和脚本化可恢复扰动产生失败及其后果，同时记录专家动作和值。3. 提出快速的分块潜在世界模型，以一次前向传播预测整段未来，并联合预测物理分解奖励、继续概率、专家价值、行为克隆动作先验和碰撞风险。4. 设计带制动单调性约束的碰撞风险头，以及将预测回报与有界风险惩罚结合的实时MPPI规划器。5. 提出在线适应机制，同时微调动力学、奖励评分器和风险头，冻结缺少在线专家标签的动作先验和值网络，并通过EMA副本稳定规划目标。6. 在CARLA和MetaDrive上进行了闭环消融、基线比较和风险预测分析，验证了风险项、在线适应及面向薄弱场景的数据飞轮的作用。
papers.relevance_cn: 与研究重点直接相关。该工作是面向自动驾驶的动作条件世界模型和闭环仿真系统：模型根据候选动作块预测未来潜状态、奖励、终止概率和碰撞风险，规划器据此在想象轨迹上选择动作并执行，再通过真实闭环驾驶收集数据进行适应。它采用因果掩码的动作条件潜在预测，保留了自回归语义，同时通过分块一次性预测16步来降低规划成本；在10Hz下用单GPU进行实时MPPI规划。其在线覆盖扩展、失败数据学习和风险感知规划与安全探索、闭环世界模型、长时域价值引导和模型复用密切相关。不过论文重点是自动驾驶控制与仿真闭环，而非视频生成、视觉视频扩散或通用长视频生成。
papers.limitations_cn: 论文的实验主要在CARLA和MetaDrive仿真器中进行，未报告真实道路或真实车辆上的验证。CARLA实验使用特权鸟瞰图和自车状态作为输入，因此不能直接代表从原始摄像头或其他传感器进行的完整自动驾驶系统。离线失败数据依赖仿真中的部分训练策略、动作噪声和人工脚本扰动，可能无法覆盖真实世界的全部失效模式。在线适应需要在训练环境中收集最多100万步交互数据；论文也指出，适应只扩展到规划器实际驾驶过的环境，在从未用于适应的城镇中收益不明显。规划预测时域仅为1.6秒，较长后果主要依赖价值头的自举。风险单调性约束在MetaDrive在线适应阶段未使用，因为其交通回放机制可能使减速导致后车追尾。SAFER的性能仍受世界模型覆盖范围和预测误差影响，论文通过数据飞轮缓解但未消除这一问题。与部分基线的比较使用不同输入或已发表结果，不能视为完整感知到控制流水线的统一比较。除上述内容外，论文未明确说明更广泛真实环境中的泛化上限。
papers.abstract_cn: 自动驾驶车辆必须预见其行动的后果，尤其是在发生碰撞的罕见且时间紧迫的情境中。世界模型能够提供这种预见能力，但其能力仅限于训练数据的覆盖范围，由此产生探索—利用困境。在覆盖范围内，规划器几乎无法超越数据；而在覆盖范围之外，模型误差会误导规划器。高水平驾驶日志很少包含能够扩大覆盖范围的失败，而通过交互学习的智能体只能通过亲自失败来获得这些经验，却不会被展示应该采取什么替代行动。我们提出SAFER框架：离线学习他人造成、经专家评判的失败，并持续从自身驾驶中在线学习。离线阶段，部分训练的智能体和脚本化的、可恢复的扰动在仿真中制造失败；专家为每个访问状态标注应采取的动作及其价值，使规划器探索的大量状态在实际驾驶前就已被覆盖。在规划阶段，分块潜在世界模型快速预见后果，从而满足实时使用要求；风险感知的基于采样的规划器则以回报减去有界碰撞惩罚来评估候选操作。在线阶段，一个循环会在驾驶超出离线数据覆盖范围的地方持续细化模型。在与对比方法进行的闭环评估中，SAFER在CARLA Leaderboard路线上的路线完成率和每步回报最高；在特权鸟瞰视角下，这两个指标分别达到0.95和0.77；在MetaDrive中，其常规交通和安全关键交通下的回合回报也最高，分别为53.4和49.0。项目主页：https://ys-qu.github.io/safer-website。

papers.title: Inertial Video World Models
papers.abstract: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant. However, many existing video world models lack an explicit mechanism for inertial state evolution, leaving the continuity of motion and structure implicit in video prediction. During autoregressive rollouts, repeated reconstruction can accumulate errors and destabilize the predicted dynamics. To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step. Central to this formulation is Inertial Memory, which turns memory from passive predictive context into an evolving video state with two complementary views: a dense Eulerian grid preserves scene-aligned evidence, while persistent Lagrangian carriers bind local content to learned canonical coordinates. At each step, the model transports the carrier content according to action-conditioned motion, predicts the complete next video state from the transported carriers and dense grid, and uses a learned gate to combine transported and newly predicted content into the memory for the next step. Extensive experiments across multiple domains, including robot manipulation, 3D game simulation, and open-world navigation, demonstrate that InertialWorld achieves competitive autoregressive prediction performance against strong video world model baselines. Codes link: https://github.com/YuanGao-YG/InertialWorld
papers.summary_cn: The physical world has inertia: it evolves from what already exists rather than being recreated at every instant.
papers.contribution_cn: To address this limitation, we introduce InertialWorld, an Inertial Video World Model that makes inertia a structural prior for autoregressive prediction: existing scene evidence is carried across time rather than reconstructed at every step.
papers.relevance_cn: 匹配研究线：world model, streaming video；关键词：world model, video world model, action-conditioned, simulation, autoregressive
papers.limitations_cn: 规则模式无法可靠判断实验质量与论文局限。

papers.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
papers.abstract: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

papers.title: SciWorldBench: Do Video World Models Really Understand Scientific Experiments?
papers.abstract: While the ability of video generation models to accurately depict scientific phenomena has received growing attention, determining whether these models genuinely understand the underlying principles remains a critical challenge. Existing benchmarks typically evaluate video samples in isolation, making it difficult to expose models that simply fit superficial visual priors. In scientific experiments, a small change in one condition produces a markedly different outcome even when the rest of the setup remains fixed. Capitalizing on this sensitivity, we introduce SciWorldBench, a benchmark comprising paired scientific experiments. Each pair varies a single condition in an otherwise fixed setup, yielding two mutually exclusive expected outcomes. Each generation prompt specifies the condition but omits the expected outcome. We evaluate ten text-and-image-to-video (TI2V) models using an independent vision-language model (VLM) that assesses each video without access to the condition text or the label identifying the correct outcome. A pair is scored as correct only when both videos depict their respective scientifically correct outcomes. Across all ten models, we find that the two videos in an experimental pair frequently depict the same outcome even though the conditions require different results. This recurring failure suggests that current video world models struggle to apply the underlying scientific principles reliably during generation. We will publicly release the benchmark dataset and open-source the evaluation code.

papers.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
papers.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

papers.title: LynnReal-Hand: Unlocking World Interaction with Hand Control
papers.abstract: Interactive video world models enable exploration through text and camera controls, yet direct object interaction requires finer control. Hands provide a natural interface, but translating continuous hand movements into coherent visual responses remains challenging because of complex hand-object dynamics and demanding real-time computation. To address these challenges, we introduce LynnReal-Hand, a hand-controlled video world model that unifies precise interaction modeling with efficient streaming generation. We curate 100K interaction clips spanning diverse real and synthetic environments and develop hand-aware supervision to improve fine-grained hand motions and object interactions. Building on this foundation, we learn a causal flow map for few-step generation and introduce region-aware score distillation that combines complementary video and image priors to refine interaction dynamics and visual appearance. To further reduce inference latency, we propose Ultra-Fast-VAE, a compact video decoder that preserves high reconstruction fidelity with substantially lower computational cost. Extensive evaluations on HandBench demonstrate superior hand-following accuracy and visual quality compared with existing approaches. Our full-sequence model achieves an FVD of 181.67 and a MANO Dice score of 93.02, while the three-step causal model maintains a MANO Dice score of 92.49. For real-time interaction, 540p streaming on a single H200 reaches 18.03 FPS with 741ms latency and an optimized peak GPU memory footprint of only 34.89GB. We will release the datasets, model weights, and the full training and inference code to support research on hand-controlled video world models.

papers.title: ScoutCache: Efficient Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Conditional Readout and Selective Caching
papers.abstract: Few-step autoregressive video diffusion enables efficient long video generation, but inference still incurs substantial computational costs from repeated denoising and KV cache operations. Existing acceleration methods reduce parts of this overhead, while historical KV reading and cache construction remain costly across video chunks. To address these challenges, we propose ScoutCache, a training-free framework that jointly optimizes denoising, historical KV reading, and cache construction. We observe that shallow feature changes provide useful information for estimating clean latent updates, while historical KV dependence varies across Transformer layers and attention heads but remains relatively stable across video chunks. Based on these observations, we develop Conditional Denoising Readout (CDR) to estimate intermediate denoising updates from shallow feature changes and known noise variations. We further introduce Output Risk Guided Historical KV Reading (ORHR) to allocate historical reading budgets based on attention output perturbations, and Content and Coverage Guided Sparse Cache Construction (CCSC) to reduce cache construction costs by selecting informative spatial tokens while maintaining spatial coverage. Extensive experiments on Self-Forcing and LongLive using VBench and MovieGen demonstrate that ScoutCache achieves up to 2.28$\times$ and 1.86$\times$ speedups, respectively, while consistently improving generation quality without modifying pretrained model parameters.

papers.title: Towards Data-Efficient, Real-Time World Models
papers.abstract: State-of-the-art world models have been used to produce sequences of gameplay that accord with provided user-input actions. However, high quality, consistent gameplay generation often comes at the cost of inference speed, making real-time interactive play and ideation challenging. The substantial quantities of data used to train state-of-the-art models have also made custom training of these models appear impractical, limiting many of their potential uses in creative fields. In this work we demonstrate a major step towards efficient world models: achieving both fast high-quality inference, and improved data efficiency. This is done by replacing the next-token prediction paradigm with a two-stage discrete diffusion-based approach, introducing a lightweight refinement transformer which carries out iterative masked predictions. Building on an autoregressive world model capable of generating highly consistent and complex sequences over minutes (Kanervisto et al., 2025), we achieve substantial model speed-up (79x) with a modest quality trade-off. Additionally, we demonstrate that this model can be trained to reproduce high-quality, consistent gameplay using a dataset containing approximately one day (28 hours) of gameplay data. Our results demonstrate progress towards removing barriers to the use of world models in settings where real-time inference and data efficiency are essential.
